reason: The narrative explicitly portrays King Zedekiah as 'doing evil in the sight of the Lord' (וַיַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה) and rebelling against the king of Babylon (וַיִּמְרֹד צִדְקִיָּהוּ בְּמֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל). The destruction, siege, and exile are presented as consequences of royal and leadership failure, not the wrongdoing of regular people. When Gedaliah offers reasonable governance and reassurance to the people, he is assassinated by Ishmael, a military leader—again demonstrating leadership failure rather than the righteousness of leaders. The narrative's structure shows God's judgment upon the nation for leadership failures, not for the wrongdoing of the regular populace. The common people are portrayed as victims and refugees responding to catastrophic circumstances created by their leaders' actions.
